intent.raw_query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter from LAX

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of Seoul's oldest and most famous traditional markets. Sample iconic Korean street foods including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap, tteokbokki, and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). Interact with local vendors and experience the vibrant atmosphere of authentic Korean market culture.

experiences.name: K-Pop & Hallyu Culture Experience in Hongdae
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Seoul's K-culture hub. Visit K-pop merchandise stores, attend a live busking performance, explore indie music venues, and try a K-pop dance class at one of the many studios in the area. Hongdae is the heartbeat of Korean youth culture and the K-wave movement.

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Experience
experiences.description: Visit the grand Gyeongbokgung Palace, the largest of Seoul's Five Grand Palaces. Rent a traditional Hanbok (Korean dress) from a nearby rental shop and explore the palace grounds for free while wearing it. Watch the ceremonial changing of the royal guard and visit the National Folk Museum of Korea located within the palace grounds.

experiences.name: Incheon Chinatown & Songwol-dong Fairy Tale Village Walk
experiences.description: Since you're based near Bupyeong-gu in Incheon, explore the nearby Incheon Chinatown — Korea's only official Chinatown — and taste jajangmyeon (black bean noodles) at its birthplace. Walk to the colorful Songwol-dong Fairy Tale Village with its whimsical murals, and stroll through the historic Open Port area to experience Incheon's unique multicultural heritage.

experiences.name: Bupyeong Modoo Mall Underground Shopping & Korean BBQ Dinner
experiences.description: Explore Bupyeong's famous underground shopping mall, one of the largest in Korea, perfect for finding K-fashion, beauty products, and accessories at local prices. End the evening at a traditional Korean BBQ restaurant in the Bupyeong area, grilling samgyeopsal (pork belly) and galbi (short ribs) tableside with soju and banchan side dishes.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Seoul, South Korea
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, then take the Airport Railroad Express (AREX) or bus to Bupyeong station. Check in to Toyoko Inn Incheon Bupyeong. Pick up a T-money card at the airport convenience store for easy transit use throughout the trip.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night snack at a 24-hour GS25 or CU convenience store near the hotel — try triangle kimbap (삼각김밥) and instant ramen for under ₩3,000

day_by_day.notes: Keep energy light tonight. Exchange some cash at the airport (Incheon has competitive rates). AREX all-stop train to Bupyeong costs around ₩1,550 with T-money. Bupyeong is a lively district with 24-hour convenience stores nearby.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from jet lag. After a late arrival, sleep in and enjoy the free breakfast if included at Toyoko Inn. Explore the immediate Bupyeong neighborhood — visit Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center (부평 지하상가), one of Korea's largest underground malls, great for affordable K-fashion and accessories.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Incheon Chinatown (인천 차이나타운) via subway — just a few stops away. Walk through the colorful archways, explore the murals, and visit the nearby Jayu Park (자유공원) for a panoramic view of Incheon port. Also check out the retro Open Port Street (개항장 거리) with its preserved colonial-era architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Sinpo International Market (신포국제시장) for street food and local snacks. Try the famous Sinpo-style chicken (신포닭강정) — sweet and spicy fried chicken unique to Incheon. Head back to the hotel early to rest up for the Seoul adventures ahead.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store (₩2,000–₩4,000)
meals.lunch: Jajangmyeon (black bean noodles) in Incheon Chinatown — authentic and cheap at around ₩7,000–₩9,000
meals.dinner: Sinpo Market street food: dakgangjeong (₩5,000), hotteok (₩1,500), and tteokbokki (₩3,000) — full meal under ₩10,000

day_by_day.notes: Dress in warm layers — average high is only 3°C in December. Incheon Chinatown is walkable from Incheon station (Line 1). Budget for the day: approximately ₩25,000–₩35,000 including transit.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway from Bupyeong to Gyeongbokgung Palace (경복궁) — about 60–70 minutes via Line 1 to Seoul Station, then Line 5 or walk. Arrive early to beat crowds. Rent a hanbok (한복) near the palace entrance for ₩15,000–₩20,000 — wearing hanbok grants FREE entry to the palace. Explore the grand palace grounds, Geunjeongjeon throne hall, and the scenic rear garden area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Bukchon Hanok Village (북촌 한옥마을) — a 15-minute walk from Gyeongbokgung. Wander the narrow alleys lined with traditional Korean hanok houses. Then head to nearby Insadong (인사동) for traditional crafts, tea houses, and K-culture souvenirs. Browse Ssamziegil (쌈지길), an artsy courtyard mall with indie shops.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Insadong's evening atmosphere and visit a traditional Korean tea house (찻집) for warm barley tea or omija tea. Head back to Bupyeong via subway. Stop at a local pojangmacha (포장마차) street stall near Bupyeong station for evening snacks.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store
meals.lunch: Gyeongbokgung area — try a set meal at a nearby Korean restaurant: doenjang jjigae (soybean paste stew) with rice for ₩8,000–₩10,000
meals.dinner: Insadong or Bupyeong pojangmacha: eomuk (fish cake skewers ₩1,000 each), tteokbokki (₩3,500), and odeng soup — under ₩10,000

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung entry is ₩3,000 normally but FREE with hanbok rental. Hanbok rental shops are clustered on the streets just outside the palace. Bring hand warmers — it will be cold standing outside. Total budget for the day: ₩40,000–₩55,000 including transit and hanbok.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Gwangjang Market (광장시장) — one of Seoul's oldest and most famous traditional markets. Arrive in the morning to see vendors setting up and enjoy a quieter atmosphere. This is a K-culture food paradise — famous for bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak kimbap (addictive mini kimbap), and yukhoe (beef tartare).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP, 동대문디자인플라자) — a futuristic landmark designed by Zaha Hadid. Explore the free outdoor areas and any free exhibitions inside. Then visit Dongdaemun History & Culture Park for a glimpse of excavated Joseon-era ruins. Browse the massive Dongdaemun shopping district for affordable K-fashion.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the famous Dongdaemun night shopping scene — the area truly comes alive after dark with wholesale and retail fashion markets. Grab street food from vendors outside the markets. Return to Bupyeong via subway.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market: mayak kimbap (₩3,000), bindaetteok (₩4,000), and a bowl of kongnamul gukbap — full satisfying lunch for ₩10,000–₩15,000
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun street food stalls: tteokbokki, sundae (blood sausage), and fried snacks — ₩8,000–₩12,000

day_by_day.notes: Gwangjang Market is on Jongno 5-ga station (Line 1). DDP is on Dongdaemun History & Culture Park station (Lines 2, 4, 5). Friday evening will be busy — great for soaking in the local energy. Budget for the day: ₩35,000–₩50,000.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Namsan Seoul Tower (남산서울타워) — take the free Namsan Cable Car (cable car costs ₩9,500 round trip) or hike up the mountain trail for free. Enjoy panoramic winter views of Seoul from the observation deck (entry ₩16,000) or admire the view from the free outdoor deck. See the famous love locks on the fence.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head down to Myeongdong (명동) — Seoul's most famous shopping and street food district. Browse cosmetics shops (Innisfree, Etude House, Olive Young) for affordable K-beauty products. The street food here is legendary — try egg bread (계란빵), hotteok, and Korean corn dogs.
day_by_day.evening: Continue exploring Myeongdong's evening street food scene — it gets even more vibrant after dark. Visit명동교자 (Myeongdong Gyoja) for their famous kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) — a Seoul institution. Return to Bupyeong via subway.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store
meals.lunch: Namsan area convenience store or packed lunch from hotel area before heading out
meals.dinner: Myeongdong Gyoja (명동교자): kalguksu ₩11,000 — hearty, warming, and iconic. Or mix street food for a similar price.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday will be very crowded in Myeongdong. Namsan cable car station is accessible from Myeongdong or Chungmuro station. The observation deck at N Seoul Tower is optional — the free outdoor terrace still offers great views. Budget for the day: ₩45,000–₩65,000.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace (창덕궁) and its UNESCO-listed Secret Garden (비원/후원). The Secret Garden tour requires a reservation and costs ₩8,000 — book in advance online. The palace itself is ₩3,000. This is one of the most beautiful and culturally rich sites in Seoul, especially with winter frost on the traditional architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Ikseon-dong Hanok Village (익선동) — a trendy neighborhood of restored hanok houses turned into cafes, vintage shops, and restaurants. Very popular with young Koreans and a great spot to experience the blend of traditional and modern K-culture. Browse the charming alleyways and pop into a cozy cafe for warmth.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Jongno 3-ga area for a traditional Korean dinner. Visit the Pimatgol alley (피맛골) area near Jonggak station — a historic alley with affordable traditional Korean restaurants. Return to Bupyeong.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store
meals.lunch: Ikseon-dong cafe lunch: Korean-style brunch or light meal at a hanok cafe — ₩10,000–₩15,000
meals.dinner: Pimatgol alley: samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup) or sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) — ₩9,000–₩13,000

day_by_day.notes: Book the Changdeokgung Secret Garden tour in advance at the official website (english.cha.go.kr). Tours run at set times and are limited. Sunday may be busy — arrive early. Budget for the day: ₩40,000–₩55,000.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (수원화성) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site about 1 hour from Bupyeong by subway (Line 1 direct to Suwon station). The fortress walls stretch 5.7 km and are free to walk. Explore the gates, watchtowers, and command posts with beautiful winter scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Suwon's Haenggung Palace (행궁) inside the fortress — entry ₩1,500. Walk the full fortress wall circuit for stunning views of the city. Explore the traditional Suwon Hwaseong Museum (₩2,000) to learn about the fortress's history and construction.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Suwon Jidong Market (지동시장) or the area near Suwon station for the famous Suwon galbi (수원갈비) — Suwon is renowned for its large, flavorful beef short ribs. Return to Bupyeong via Line 1.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store before departing
meals.lunch: Suwon traditional market near the fortress: bibimbap or gukbap for ₩7,000–₩9,000
meals.dinner: Suwon galbi restaurant near Suwon station — budget around ₩15,000–₩20,000 for a satisfying portion

day_by_day.notes: Suwon is directly accessible from Bupyeong on Line 1 — no transfers needed. The fortress walk takes 2–3 hours at a leisurely pace. Wear very warm shoes as the fortress walls are exposed and windy in December. Budget for the day: ₩35,000–₩50,000.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Hongdae (홍대) — Seoul's vibrant university district known for indie music, street art, K-pop culture, and youth fashion. Visit the Hongdae Free Market area (weekends are best but the neighborhood is lively daily). Browse the unique shops along Eoulmadang-ro and the surrounding streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Sinchon (신촌) and Ewha Womans University (이화여자대학교) — the campus is architecturally stunning and free to enter. The ECC (Ewha Campus Complex) underground building is a remarkable piece of modern architecture. Browse the Ewha shopping street for affordable K-fashion and accessories.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hongdae for the evening — the area transforms at night with buskers, street performers, and live music. Visit a norebang (노래방 / karaoke room) for a quintessential K-culture experience — small rooms cost ₩10,000–₩15,000 per hour for a group. Return to Bupyeong.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store
meals.lunch: Hongdae area: Korean fried chicken and beer (chimaek 치맥) at a local spot — ₩12,000–₩15,000, or a cheaper kimbap restaurant for ₩5,000–₩7,000
meals.dinner: Sinchon or Hongdae: budae jjigae (army stew — a Korean-American fusion stew) — ₩10,000–₩13,000 per person, great for cold weather

day_by_day.notes: Hongdae station is on Lines 2, Airport Railroad, and Gyeongui-Jungang Line. The neighborhood is best experienced in the afternoon and evening. Norebang is a must-do K-culture experience — look for 'coin norebang' (코인노래방) for solo singing at ₩500–₩1,000 per song. Budget for the day: ₩45,000–₩65,000.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple (조계사) — the head temple of Korean Buddhism, located in central Seoul and FREE to enter. The temple is beautifully decorated for the winter season. Attend a morning ceremony if timing allows. Nearby, explore the Buddhist cultural street with shops selling prayer beads, incense, and traditional crafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Cheonggyecheon Stream (청계천) — a restored urban stream running through central Seoul. Walk along the stream path, admire the winter decorations (often lit up for the holiday season), and enjoy the peaceful contrast to the busy city above. Walk toward City Hall Plaza (서울광장) which often has a winter ice skating rink (₩1,000 skate rental).
day_by_day.evening: Visit Deoksugung Palace (덕수궁) for the famous Moonlight Tour or evening walk — the palace is beautifully lit at night. The Deoksugung Stonewall Walkway (돌담길) is a romantic and atmospheric evening stroll. Nearby Euljiro (을지로) has a thriving local bar and restaurant scene — explore the retro alleyways.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store
meals.lunch: Insadong or Jogyesa area: temple food restaurant (사찰음식) for a unique vegetarian Buddhist meal experience — ₩10,000–₩15,000
meals.dinner: Euljiro pojangmacha or local restaurant: gopchang (grilled intestines) or makguksu (buckwheat noodles) — ₩10,000–₩15,000

day_by_day.notes: December 23rd — Seoul will be festively decorated for Christmas. Cheonggyecheon often has special winter light festivals. City Hall ice rink is seasonal — check availability. Deoksugung entry is ₩1,000. Budget for the day: ₩35,000–₩50,000.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Lotte World (롯데월드) in Jamsil — one of the world's largest indoor theme parks. Entry is ₩62,000 for adults (Magic Pass) but you can opt for just the free outdoor area (Lotte World Adventure outdoor section) or visit the adjacent Seokchon Lake (석촌호수) which is completely free and beautifully decorated for Christmas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Jamsil area — visit Lotte World Mall (free to browse) and the observation deck of Lotte World Tower (롯데월드타워) — the 5th tallest building in the world. The Seoul Sky observation deck costs ₩27,000 but the view is spectacular. Alternatively, enjoy the free lake walk and Christmas atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul is a major celebration — head to Myeongdong or Hongdae for the festive atmosphere. Streets are packed with couples and families, Christmas lights are everywhere, and street food vendors are in full force. Enjoy the uniquely Korean Christmas Eve experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store
meals.lunch: Jamsil area: affordable Korean set meal near Lotte World — ₩9,000–₩12,000
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve street food feast in Myeongdong or Hongdae — budget ₩15,000–₩20,000 for a variety of street foods and a warm drink

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is one of the busiest nights in Seoul — expect large crowds in entertainment districts. Seokchon Lake is FREE and beautifully lit — a great budget alternative to paid attractions. Subway will be crowded late at night. Budget for the day: ₩50,000–₩80,000 depending on attraction choices.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Bukhansan National Park (북한산국립공원) for a winter hiking experience — one of the most popular urban national parks in the world. Take the subway to Gupabal or Dobongsan station. Entry to the park is FREE. Choose a beginner-friendly trail like the Bukhansanseong Fortress trail for stunning winter mountain views and ancient fortress walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking or descend and explore the mountain village area at the base of the park. Visit a traditional Korean mountain rest stop (산장) for warm sikhye (sweet rice drink) or doenjang jjigae. Return to central Seoul or head back toward Bupyeong.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate Christmas evening Korean-style — visit a local Korean BBQ restaurant (삼겹살 집) for a festive dinner. Samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly) is a beloved Korean social dining experience. Many Koreans celebrate Christmas with fried chicken and beer — try this local tradition.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or pack convenience store snacks for the hike
meals.lunch: Mountain trail snacks or a warm meal at a mountain village restaurant near the park entrance — doenjang jjigae set ₩9,000
meals.dinner: Korean BBQ: samgyeopsal restaurant — ₩15,000–₩20,000 per person including meat, sides, and a drink

day_by_day.notes: Bukhansan in winter can be icy — wear hiking boots with good grip and bring hand warmers. The park is FREE but some facilities may charge small fees. Christmas Day is a public holiday in Korea — most attractions are open. Budget for the day: ₩35,000–₩50,000.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Folk Museum of Korea (국립민속박물관) — located within the Gyeongbokgung Palace grounds. Entry is FREE. This museum offers an excellent deep-dive into Korean traditional culture, customs, and daily life across the centuries. Perfect for K-culture enthusiasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Itaewon (이태원) — Seoul's most international neighborhood. Visit the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art (리움미술관) for world-class Korean and international art — entry ₩10,000. Explore the Itaewon antique street and the trendy Haebangchon (해방촌) neighborhood on the hillside for unique cafes and local vibes.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Itaewon's diverse dining scene for your last full evening meal splurge. Then head to Han River Park (한강공원) — Banpo or Yeouido section — for a nighttime walk along the river. The Banpo Bridge Rainbow Fountain (반포대교 달빛무지개분수) may not operate in winter, but the river views are still beautiful. Return to Bupyeong.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store
meals.lunch: Gyeongbokgung area: affordable Korean restaurant — bibimbap ₩9,000–₩11,000
meals.dinner: Itaewon: treat yourself to a slightly nicer meal — Korean-Western fusion or a quality Korean restaurant — budget ₩15,000–₩25,000

day_by_day.notes: The National Folk Museum is FREE and excellent — allow 2 hours. Itaewon is accessible from Itaewon station (Line 6). Han River parks are free and open 24 hours — dress very warmly for an evening riverside walk in December. Budget for the day: ₩45,000–₩65,000.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul — revisit any favorite spots or do last-minute souvenir shopping. Head to Namdaemun Market (남대문시장) — Korea's largest traditional market, open early. Great for affordable souvenirs: dried seaweed, gochujang, instant ramyeon sets, Korean snacks, and accessories. Bargaining is acceptable here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pack up and check out of Toyoko Inn. Store luggage at the hotel or at a nearby coin locker. Take one last stroll through Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center for any final purchases. Head to Incheon Airport via AREX or bus — allow at least 2–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport. Enjoy a final Korean meal at the airport — try the food court on the departure level for affordable Korean options like bibimbap or ramyeon before your flight.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store — last Korean convenience store meal!
meals.lunch: Namdaemun Market: hotteok (₩1,500), kalguksu (₩8,000), or a market snack spread — ₩10,000–₩15,000
meals.dinner: Incheon Airport food court: Korean set meal — ₩10,000–₩15,000

day_by_day.notes: Namdaemun Market is near City Hall or Hoehyeon station (Line 4). Best souvenirs to buy: Korean instant noodles, gochujang paste, dried seaweed (김), Korean snack packs, and cosmetics from Olive Young. Keep T-money card — it can be refunded at the airport or kept for a future trip. Allow plenty of time for airport transit. Safe travels!

trip_options.title: Classic Seoul, South Korea Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, collect baggage, then take the Airport Railroad Express (AREX) or a limousine bus to Bupyeong station area. Check in to Toyoko Inn Incheon Bupyeong and settle into your room.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at a 24-hour convenience store (GS25 or CU) near the hotel — try triangle kimbap, instant ramen, or hotteok for a quick, affordable bite after arrival.

day_by_day.notes: Dress warmly — December temperatures average around 3°C. Pick up a T-money card at the airport convenience store or ticket machine for easy transit use throughout the trip. Exchange some cash (KRW) at the airport for better rates. Rest well tonight as Day 2 begins your full exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Start your first full day with a walk around Bupyeong Modoo Mall and Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center, one of Korea's largest underground markets. Browse K-fashion, accessories, and local goods. Get a feel for everyday Korean shopping culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway (Line 1) from Bupyeong to Incheon Chinatown and Sinpo International Market. Explore the colorful murals, Chinese-Korean fusion architecture, and the nearby Jayu Park — Korea's first Western-style park with great views of the port. Walk along the Open Port Area to see colonial-era buildings.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Sinpo International Market for evening street food. The market is famous for Sinpo-style dakgangjeong (sweet crispy fried chicken). Stroll the lit-up market stalls before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby bakery like Paris Baguette — try a warm pastry and coffee (around 5,000–8,000 KRW).
meals.lunch: Jajangmyeon (black bean noodles) or tangsuyuk (sweet and sour pork) at one of the authentic Chinese-Korean restaurants in Incheon Chinatown (10,000–15,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Sinpo dakgangjeong and tteokbokki at Sinpo International Market stalls (8,000–12,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: Wear layers and a warm coat. The underground shopping center is a great way to stay warm while exploring. Bupyeong and Incheon Chinatown are easily connected by subway Line 1 — about 10 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Bupyeong to central Seoul via subway (Line 1 to Seoul Station, approx. 40–50 min). Head to Gyeongbokgung Palace, the grandest of Seoul's Five Grand Palaces. Catch the 10:00 AM Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at the main gate. Rent a hanbok (traditional Korean dress) from a nearby rental shop to enter the palace for free and take stunning photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk north to Bukchon Hanok Village, a beautifully preserved neighborhood of traditional Korean hanok houses. Wander the narrow alleys, enjoy the contrast of old architecture against the modern city skyline, and visit small craft shops and galleries. Continue to Insadong for a leisurely afternoon browsing antique shops, tea houses, and K-culture souvenir stores.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Insadong's Ssamziegil — an open-air courtyard mall with indie shops, art installations, and street food. Enjoy the festive December atmosphere with holiday lights.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store onigiri and coffee before departing.
meals.lunch: Traditional Korean set meal (한정식 hanjeongsik lite) near Gyeongbokgung — try bibimbap or doenjang jjigae at a local restaurant (10,000–15,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a cozy restaurant in Insadong — try samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly) at a mid-range BBQ spot (15,000–20,000 KRW per person).

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays. Hanbok rental shops near the palace charge around 10,000–20,000 KRW for 2 hours. Bukchon Hanok Village asks visitors to be quiet out of respect for residents. Carry hand warmers — it will be cold walking outdoors.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Namsan Mountain and N Seoul Tower. Take the Namsan Cable Car up for panoramic winter views of Seoul. Visit the famous love lock fence and enjoy the crisp morning air. The tower area is magical in December with holiday decorations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and make your way to Myeongdong, Seoul's most famous shopping and beauty district. Explore K-beauty stores (Innisfree, Etude House, Olive Young), fashion boutiques, and the lively street food scene. This is the heart of Korean pop culture commerce.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Myeongdong for the evening street food experience — one of the best in Seoul. The street vendors light up at night and the energy is electric even in winter.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast near the hotel or at a café in Myeongdong before heading to Namsan.
meals.lunch: Street food lunch in Myeongdong — try hotteok (sweet pancake), eomuk (fish cake skewers), and gyeran-ppang (egg bread) from vendors (5,000–10,000 KRW total).
meals.dinner: Sit-down dinner at a Myeongdong restaurant — try naengmyeon (cold buckwheat noodles) or galbitang (short rib soup) to warm up (12,000–18,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: N Seoul Tower admission is around 21,000 KRW for adults. The cable car costs about 9,500 KRW round trip. Myeongdong is extremely popular — expect crowds on Friday evening. Olive Young is a must-visit for K-beauty products at reasonable prices.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and its famous Secret Garden (Huwon). This UNESCO World Heritage Site is one of Seoul's most beautiful palaces, especially with winter frost on the traditional architecture. Book the Secret Garden tour in advance (guided tours only, limited spots).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Changgyeonggung Palace or head to the Jongno area to explore Tapgol Park and the traditional Jongno street. Visit Jogyesa Temple, the head temple of Korean Buddhism, beautifully decorated with lanterns for the winter season.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Cheonggyecheon Stream for a romantic evening walk along the illuminated waterway. The stream is lit up beautifully in winter and is a peaceful escape from the busy city streets.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Korean breakfast at a local sikdang (식당) near the hotel — try haejang-guk (hangover soup) or congee (juk) (8,000–12,000 KRW).
meals.lunch: Lunch near Changdeokgung — try a warm sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) at a local restaurant (9,000–13,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Dinner in the Jongno area — try dakhanmari (whole chicken in broth) at the famous Dakhanmari Alley near Dongdaemun (15,000–20,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: Changdeokgung Secret Garden tours must be booked online in advance at the palace website. Tours are available in English. Wear very warm shoes as you'll be walking on stone paths. Cheonggyecheon Stream is free to visit and accessible from multiple subway stations.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — Zaha Hadid's iconic futuristic building. Visit the design exhibitions and the surrounding Dongdaemun History & Culture Park. The area is fascinating for its blend of ancient city wall ruins and ultra-modern architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Gwangjang Market, one of Seoul's oldest and most authentic traditional markets. This is a paradise for local food lovers — browse the fabric stalls and food hall packed with grandmothers cooking traditional dishes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Dongdaemun for the famous night shopping experience. Dongdaemun's fashion malls (Doota, Migliore) open late and are buzzing on Sunday evenings. Browse K-fashion at wholesale and retail prices.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast near the hotel — try a Korean-style egg sandwich and Americano at a local café (6,000–9,000 KRW).
meals.lunch: Iconic lunch at Gwangjang Market — must-try bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak kimbap (addictive mini kimbap), and yukhoe (beef tartare). Budget around 10,000–15,000 KRW.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a restaurant near Dongdaemun — try gopchang (grilled intestines) or a hearty Korean stew (13,000–18,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: DDP admission varies by exhibition — check the website for current shows. Gwangjang Market is busiest at lunch and is a must for authentic Korean food culture. Dongdaemun shopping malls are open until 4–5 AM, so no rush in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress, a UNESCO World Heritage Site about 1 hour from Bupyeong by subway. Walk along the impressive 5.7 km fortress walls that encircle the old city. The winter scenery with frost on the stone walls is stunning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's Haenggung Palace (Hwaseong Haenggung) inside the fortress grounds. Visit the Suwon Traditional Culture Center to learn about local crafts and history. Browse the traditional market street near the fortress.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Bupyeong/Incheon area. Spend a relaxed evening near the hotel, exploring the local Bupyeong neighborhood — visit a jjimjilbang (Korean sauna/bathhouse) for a warm, relaxing evening experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store before departing for Suwon.
meals.lunch: Suwon galbi (Suwon-style short ribs) — the city's most famous dish — at a local restaurant near the fortress (15,000–25,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Jjimjilbang restaurant or a nearby Korean restaurant in Bupyeong — try kimchi jjigae or budae jjigae (army stew) (10,000–15,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: Suwon Hwaseong Fortress admission is around 1,000 KRW. Take subway Line 1 from Bupyeong directly to Suwon Station (about 50 minutes). A jjimjilbang entry costs around 10,000–15,000 KRW and includes access to hot baths, saunas, and rest areas — perfect for warming up after a cold day.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Hongdae (Hongik University area) — the epicenter of Korean youth culture, indie music, and street art. Explore the vibrant murals, quirky cafés, and K-pop culture shops. Visit the Trick Eye Museum or LINE Friends Store for fun K-culture experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Sinchon and Ewha Womans University area. The Ewha campus is architecturally stunning with its famous underground ECC building. Browse the trendy shops and cafés in Sinchon, popular with university students.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hongdae for the evening — the neighborhood truly comes alive at night with buskers, live music, and street performances. Visit a norebang (karaoke room) for an authentic K-culture experience.

meals.breakfast: Trendy café breakfast in Hongdae — try a Korean-style brunch at one of the many Instagram-worthy cafés (8,000–13,000 KRW).
meals.lunch: Lunch in Hongdae — try tteokbokki and sundae (blood sausage) at a pojangmacha (street tent) or a casual restaurant (8,000–12,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a Hongdae restaurant — try yangnyeom chicken (Korean fried chicken) with a cold Hite beer at a local chimaek spot (15,000–20,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: Norebang rooms cost around 15,000–25,000 KRW per hour for a private room. Hongdae is very lively on weekday evenings — expect street performers even in December. The Trick Eye Museum costs around 15,000 KRW. Hongdae is accessible via subway Line 2 or the AREX airport line.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Itaewon and the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art — one of Korea's finest private art museums featuring both traditional Korean art and contemporary international works. The building itself, designed by three world-renowned architects, is a masterpiece.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Itaewon's multicultural neighborhood — browse the international restaurants, vintage clothing shops, and antique stores on Antique Furniture Street. Walk up to Haebangchon (HBC) for a more local, artsy vibe with independent cafés and boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gangnam district for the evening. Visit COEX Mall — one of Asia's largest underground shopping malls — and the famous COEX Starfield Library, a stunning public library inside the mall. Browse the bookstore and enjoy the festive Christmas decorations.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast near the hotel before heading out — try a warm bowl of seolleongtang (ox bone soup) at a local restaurant (9,000–12,000 KRW).
meals.lunch: International lunch in Itaewon — try a Korean-Mexican fusion burrito or a Middle Eastern shawarma for a multicultural experience (10,000–15,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Dinner in Gangnam — try a modern Korean restaurant or a trendy ramen shop near COEX (13,000–20,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: Leeum Museum admission is around 10,000 KRW. COEX Starfield Library is free to visit and is one of Seoul's most photogenic spots. Gangnam is accessible via subway Line 2. The area will be beautifully decorated for Christmas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Bukhansan National Park for a morning winter hike. The mountain park sits within Seoul city limits and offers spectacular views of the snow-dusted peaks and the city below. Choose a beginner-friendly trail like the Bukhansanseong Fortress trail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and head to Myeongdong Cathedral — Seoul's most iconic Catholic church, beautifully lit for Christmas Eve. The area around the cathedral will be festively decorated. Browse the Christmas markets and enjoy the holiday atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Christmas Eve in Seoul — the city goes all out with lights and celebrations. Head to Cheonggyecheon Stream or City Hall Plaza for the Christmas light festival. Many young Koreans celebrate Christmas Eve like Valentine's Day, making the city especially lively.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the hike — convenience store kimbap and hot coffee or a quick meal near the hotel.
meals.lunch: Post-hike warm meal near Bukhansan — try a hearty doenjang jjigae or kimchi jjigae at a mountain restaurant (10,000–15,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve dinner — treat yourself to a Korean BBQ restaurant in Myeongdong or a nice Korean fusion restaurant (20,000–30,000 KRW per person).

day_by_day.notes: Bukhansan National Park is free to enter. Wear proper hiking boots and warm layers — trails can be icy in December. Bring crampons or ice grips for shoes if possible. Christmas Eve in Seoul is very romantic and festive — the city is beautifully illuminated. Book dinner in advance if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeonghuigung Palace (less crowded than Gyeongbokgung) and the Seoul Museum of History next door. Learn about Seoul's transformation from ancient Joseon capital to modern megacity through fascinating exhibits. The museum is free to enter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Seochon Village (west of Gyeongbokgung) — a charming neighborhood of traditional hanok houses converted into cafés, art galleries, and boutiques. This is a quieter, more authentic alternative to Bukchon. Visit the Yun Dong-ju Literary Museum.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Lotte World Tower in Jamsil for the evening. Visit the Sky Observatory on the 117th–123rd floors for breathtaking nighttime views of Seoul. The tower and surrounding Lotte World Mall are spectacularly lit for Christmas.

meals.breakfast: Christmas morning café breakfast — try a festive holiday drink and pastry at a cozy Seochon café (8,000–12,000 KRW).
meals.lunch: Lunch in Seochon Village — try a traditional Korean meal at a hanok café-restaurant (12,000–18,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Christmas dinner near Lotte World — try a nice Korean or international restaurant in the Jamsil area (20,000–30,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: Seoul Museum of History is free. Lotte World Tower Sky Observatory costs around 27,000 KRW. Many restaurants may have special Christmas menus — check in advance. Christmas Day is a public holiday in South Korea, so some smaller shops may be closed but major attractions remain open.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan — one of the largest museums in Asia, with an incredible collection of Korean artifacts spanning thousands of years. The museum is free and takes 2–3 hours to explore properly. Don't miss the Goryeo celadon and Joseon white porcelain collections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the War Memorial of Korea nearby — a powerful and moving museum documenting Korea's military history, including the Korean War. The outdoor exhibits with tanks, aircraft, and warships are impressive even in winter. Free admission.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your last full evening in the Yongsan Electronics Market or head back to a favorite neighborhood for final shopping and souvenir hunting. Visit a traditional Korean tea house for a warm, reflective end to your trip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local bakery near the hotel for a relaxed morning start.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the National Museum of Korea's cafeteria or a nearby restaurant — try a Korean set meal (10,000–15,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner — splurge slightly on a memorable Korean meal. Try a traditional Korean royal cuisine restaurant or a premium Korean BBQ spot (25,000–35,000 KRW per person).

day_by_day.notes: Both the National Museum of Korea and the War Memorial are free. The National Museum is closed on Mondays. Allow at least 2 hours for each museum. This is a great day for reflection on Korean history and culture before your trip ends. Pack souvenirs tonight to prepare for departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — take a leisurely walk around the Bupyeong neighborhood. Visit a local juk (porridge) restaurant for a light, healthy Korean breakfast. Do any last-minute shopping at Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center for affordable K-fashion and accessories.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, visit a nearby café for a final Korean coffee experience. Pack and check out of the hotel. Head to Incheon International Airport via AREX or limousine bus (allow 60–90 minutes from Bupyeong). Use remaining KRW at the airport duty-free shops.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Incheon International Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days of K-culture, incredible food, and unforgettable experiences in Seoul and Incheon.

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast — try juk (rice porridge) with various toppings at a local porridge restaurant (8,000–12,000 KRW).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport — try a Korean meal at one of the many airport restaurants before departure (12,000–18,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: On the plane or at the airport depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time at Toyoko Inn is typically 11:00 AM — confirm with the hotel. Incheon Airport is one of the world's best airports with excellent shopping, dining, and cultural experiences (free Korean cultural performances and craft workshops in the transit area). Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before international departure. T-money card can be refunded at the airport.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Seoul, South Korea Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of Seoul's oldest and most famous traditional markets. Sample iconic Korean street foods including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap, tteokbokki, and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). Interact with local vendors and experience the vibrant atmosphere of authentic Korean market culture.

experiences.name: K-Pop & Hallyu Culture Experience in Hongdae
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Seoul's K-culture hub. Visit K-pop merchandise stores, attend a live busking performance, explore indie music venues, and try a K-pop dance class at one of the many studios in the area. Hongdae is the heartbeat of Korean youth culture and the K-wave movement.

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Experience
experiences.description: Visit the grand Gyeongbokgung Palace, the largest of Seoul's Five Grand Palaces. Rent a traditional Hanbok (Korean dress) from a nearby rental shop and explore the palace grounds for free while wearing it. Watch the ceremonial changing of the royal guard and visit the National Folk Museum of Korea located within the palace grounds.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and arrange a pre-booked premium airport limousine or private transfer to Toyoko Inn Incheon Bupyeong. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room.

meals.breakfast: N/A – In flight
meals.lunch: N/A – In flight
meals.dinner: Late-night arrival snack at the hotel or a quick visit to a nearby 24-hour convenience store (GS25 or CU) for Korean ramyeon, kimbap, and hot drinks to tide you over until morning.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light – you've just landed after a long flight. Confirm your hotel reservation in advance and pre-arrange a private airport transfer for a seamless, premium arrival experience. The Bupyeong area has several 24-hour eateries if you're hungry after check-in.

day_by_day.morning: After a well-deserved rest, enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Then explore the Bupyeong area – stroll through Bupyeong Modoo Mall underground shopping arcade, one of Korea's largest underground markets, to get your bearings and pick up any essentials. Take the subway (Line 1) toward central Incheon's Chinatown and Jayu Park for a scenic morning walk with views over the port city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel into Seoul via subway or private car (approx. 40–50 min). Begin your Seoul orientation with a visit to Insadong, Seoul's premier cultural district. Browse high-end traditional craft galleries, antique shops, and the Ssamziegil courtyard complex. Visit Jogyesa Temple, the head temple of Korean Buddhism, beautifully decorated with winter lanterns for the season.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Bukchon Hanok Village for a magical twilight walk through preserved traditional Korean hanok houses. The narrow alleyways lit by warm lantern light are especially atmospheric in winter. End the evening with dinner in nearby Anguk.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Café Bora in Insadong for premium Korean-style breakfast with traditional teas and pastries.
meals.lunch: Sanchon Restaurant in Insadong – a legendary temple food restaurant serving elaborate multi-course vegetarian Buddhist cuisine in a beautifully decorated traditional setting.
meals.dinner: Tosokchon Samgyetang (Anguk area) – famous for premium ginseng chicken soup (samgyetang), a warming and nourishing dish perfect for cold December evenings.

day_by_day.notes: Dress in warm layers – December highs are around 3°C. Comfortable walking shoes are essential for Bukchon's hilly alleyways. Consider purchasing a T-money card at the airport or hotel for seamless subway travel throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Experience – Arrive early (9:00 AM) at Gyeongbokgung Palace, the grandest of Seoul's Five Grand Palaces. Rent a premium hanbok (traditional Korean garment) from a nearby high-end rental shop such as Hanboknam or Gyeongbokgung Hanbok Rental for free palace entry. Explore the vast palace grounds, Geunjeongjeon throne hall, and the serene Hyangwonjeong pavilion dusted with winter frost.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the adjacent National Folk Museum of Korea (free entry with hanbok) for an immersive deep-dive into Korean history and culture. Afterward, visit Gyeonghuigung Palace and the Seoul Museum of History nearby for additional cultural context. Return hanbok by the designated time and warm up with a hot beverage at a nearby café.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Cheonggyecheon Stream for a romantic winter evening stroll along the illuminated urban waterway. The stream is beautifully lit in December. Continue to the nearby Gwanghwamun Square to see the iconic Admiral Yi Sun-sin statue and King Sejong statue, often decorated for the winter season.

meals.breakfast: Gwanghwamun Jip – a classic Korean breakfast spot near the palace serving doenjang jjigae (fermented soybean paste stew) and rice, a true local morning experience.
meals.lunch: Jihwaja – a premium Korean royal cuisine restaurant near Gyeongbokgung, serving beautifully presented dishes inspired by Joseon Dynasty court food.
meals.dinner: Mingles (Gangnam) or Jungsik – both Michelin-starred restaurants offering modern Korean cuisine. Book well in advance. Alternatively, Gwanghwamun Haenyeo for premium raw seafood and Korean traditional dishes.

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung Palace opens at 9:00 AM and is closed on Tuesdays. The Changing of the Royal Guard ceremony takes place at 10:00 AM and 2:00 PM – don't miss it. Hanbok rental shops open around 9:00 AM; book ahead during peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour – Head to Gwangjang Market, one of Seoul's oldest and most iconic traditional markets (est. 1905). Join a guided premium street food tour or explore independently. Must-try items include bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (addictive mini rice rolls), yukhoe (Korean beef tartare), and mung bean jelly. The market is especially vibrant in the morning when vendors are at their freshest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearby Ikseon-dong Hanok Village, a trendy neighborhood of restored hanok houses converted into chic cafés, boutiques, and galleries. Browse artisan shops and enjoy the contrast of traditional architecture with contemporary Seoul culture. Visit a premium Korean tea house for a traditional tea ceremony experience.
day_by_day.evening: Travel to Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) – Zaha Hadid's futuristic landmark – for an evening visit. Explore any current design exhibitions or fashion showcases. The illuminated exterior is stunning at night. Browse the surrounding Dongdaemun fashion district.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel before heading to Gwangjang Market early.
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market – indulge in a full spread of traditional street foods as your lunch experience. Budget approximately ₩30,000–50,000 for a generous tasting spread.
meals.dinner: Hanilkwan in Insadong or Jung Sikdang – premium Korean traditional cuisine with refined presentations. Alternatively, Balwoo Gongyang near Jogyesa Temple for an exquisite temple food dinner experience.

day_by_day.notes: Gwangjang Market is busiest and most atmospheric in the morning and early afternoon. Bring cash as many vendors prefer it. Ikseon-dong is a short walk or quick taxi ride from the market. DDP is open until 9:00 PM for exhibitions.

day_by_day.morning: K-Pop & Hallyu Culture Experience in Hongdae – Travel to Hongdae, Seoul's vibrant youth and K-culture hub. Start with a visit to K-pop merchandise flagship stores including SM Town COEX (or SM's Hongdae store), Big Hit / HYBE Insight Museum, and YG Republic. Browse limited-edition albums, photocards, and exclusive merchandise. Visit a K-pop photo booth studio for fun commemorative photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Hallyu experience with a visit to the HYBE Insight Museum (Yongsan) – an immersive, premium museum dedicated to BTS and HYBE artists with interactive exhibitions, rare memorabilia, and behind-the-scenes content. Book tickets in advance as they sell out quickly. Afterward, explore the surrounding Yongsan electronics district.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hongdae for the evening busking performances – local and aspiring K-pop artists perform live on the streets, especially on weekends. The atmosphere is electric. Explore the vibrant nightlife, neon-lit streets, and K-culture cafés including character-themed and idol-themed establishments.

meals.breakfast: % Arabica or Fritz Coffee Company near Hongdae for a premium specialty coffee and pastry breakfast.
meals.lunch: Maple Tree House (Itaewon or Mapo) – premium Korean BBQ with USDA prime and Hanwoo beef, a luxurious midday feast.
meals.dinner: Yeonnam-dong neighborhood near Hongdae – explore the trendy restaurant strip. Recommended: Onjium for refined modern Korean cuisine, or Poom Seoul for a premium Korean tasting menu experience.

day_by_day.notes: HYBE Insight Museum requires advance online booking – check availability before the trip. Weekend evenings in Hongdae are very lively but can be crowded; embrace the energy as part of the authentic K-culture experience. Dress warmly as you'll be spending time outdoors watching busking performances.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and its UNESCO-listed Secret Garden (Huwon). The Secret Garden tour is guided and limited in numbers – book in advance. The winter landscape of bare trees, frozen ponds, and traditional pavilions is hauntingly beautiful. This is considered the most beautiful of Seoul's palaces.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Changgyeonggung Palace next door (connected ticket available) and then walk through the historic Naksan Park area for panoramic views of Seoul's old city walls and the surrounding hanok neighborhoods. Visit the Ihwa Mural Village on the slopes of Naksan for street art and local culture.
day_by_day.evening: Head to N Seoul Tower (Namsan Tower) via cable car for a spectacular panoramic night view of Seoul's glittering winter skyline. Visit the observation deck and enjoy the romantic lock wall tradition. Have dinner at the tower's revolving restaurant for an unforgettable dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Café Onion Anguk – a beautifully restored hanok café serving artisan pastries and specialty coffee, perfect before the palace visit.
meals.lunch: Jirisan – a premium mountain vegetable and Korean traditional cuisine restaurant in the Insadong/Anguk area.
meals.dinner: N Grill Revolving Restaurant at N Seoul Tower – a premium dining experience with 360-degree views of Seoul. The set menu features Korean-Western fusion cuisine. Reservations essential.

day_by_day.notes: Changdeokgung Secret Garden tours are conducted in Korean and English at set times – the English tour is typically at 11:30 AM. Book online at the palace website. The cable car to Namsan Tower runs until 11:00 PM. Bring a padlock to add to the famous lock wall.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the DMZ (Demilitarized Zone) – Book a premium guided DMZ tour departing from central Seoul. Visit the Joint Security Area (JSA) at Panmunjom, the Third Infiltration Tunnel, Dora Observatory, and Dorasan Station. This is one of the most historically significant and unique experiences available in South Korea, offering a sobering glimpse into the divided Korean Peninsula.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the DMZ tour with the afternoon portion, including the Imjingak Peace Park and the Bridge of Freedom. Return to Seoul by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Recover from the emotionally impactful day with a relaxing evening in Itaewon or the upscale Hannam-dong neighborhood. Browse international boutiques, art galleries, and concept stores. Enjoy a quiet, premium dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before the DMZ tour departure (tours typically depart by 7:30–8:00 AM from central Seoul).
meals.lunch: Lunch is typically included or arranged as part of the premium DMZ tour package near the Imjingak area.
meals.dinner: Vatos Urban Tacos (Itaewon) for a fun Korean-Mexican fusion experience, or Gaon (Gangnam) for an ultra-premium Korean fine dining experience – one of Seoul's most celebrated restaurants with three Michelin stars.

day_by_day.notes: JSA tours require passport and advance booking – spaces are limited and tours can be cancelled due to military/political situations. Book through a reputable operator such as USO Tours or Koridoor. Dress respectfully (no ripped jeans or revealing clothing) as per military zone regulations.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the upscale Gangnam district – start with a morning walk along the tree-lined Garosu-gil (Tree-lined Road), a chic boulevard of high-end boutiques, concept stores, art galleries, and premium cafés. Browse Korean designer fashion and lifestyle brands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit COEX Mall and the stunning COEX Starfield Library – one of Seoul's most Instagrammable spaces with floor-to-ceiling bookshelves. Explore the SM Town COEX Artium for K-pop culture. Visit the Bongeunsa Temple adjacent to COEX for a peaceful contrast to the surrounding modernity – the temple is beautifully decorated for the winter season.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the glittering Gangnam nightscape. Visit the Lotte World Tower Sky Observatory (123 floors, 555m) for the highest views in Korea. The observation deck offers breathtaking night views of Seoul. Afterward, explore the Lotte World Mall's premium dining and entertainment options.

meals.breakfast: Tartine Manufactory or a premium Garosu-gil café for artisan coffee and freshly baked pastries.
meals.lunch: Hanwoo House or Dons Bogam in Gangnam – premium Korean Hanwoo (Korean native beef) BBQ, considered among the finest beef in the world.
meals.dinner: Jungsik Seoul (Cheongdam) – a two-Michelin-star modern Korean restaurant offering an innovative tasting menu. One of Seoul's most prestigious dining experiences. Reservations essential.

day_by_day.notes: Lotte World Tower Sky Observatory tickets can be purchased online in advance. The COEX Starfield Library is free to enter and open during mall hours. Bongeunsa Temple is free to enter and particularly atmospheric in the evening with lantern lighting.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan – one of Asia's largest museums with an extraordinary collection of Korean art, history, and artifacts spanning thousands of years. Highlights include the Gilt-bronze Maitreya Bodhisattva and the Celadon collection. The museum is free to enter and world-class in presentation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the War Memorial of Korea nearby – a powerful and comprehensive museum documenting Korea's military history, including the Korean War. The outdoor exhibition of military equipment and the moving memorial wall are particularly impactful. Afterward, stroll through the upscale Itaewon Antique Furniture Street for unique Korean antiques and art.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the vibrant Myeongdong district for evening shopping and street food. Browse Korean beauty flagship stores (Sulwhasoo, History of Whoo, Innisfree) for premium K-beauty products. Experience the festive Christmas atmosphere as Myeongdong is beautifully decorated in late December.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby café in Bupyeong before traveling to Yongsan.
meals.lunch: Noryangjin Fish Market – visit Seoul's famous wholesale fish market and choose your own fresh seafood to be prepared on-site at the upstairs restaurants. A truly immersive and premium seafood experience.
meals.dinner: Myeongdong Kyoja – the legendary hand-made noodle and dumpling restaurant, an institution since 1966. Queue is worth it. Alternatively, Gogung in Myeongdong for premium Jeonju-style bibimbap served in a traditional setting.

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Korea is closed on Mondays. Noryangjin Fish Market is most vibrant in the morning but operates throughout the day. Myeongdong is extremely busy in the evenings, especially pre-Christmas – embrace the festive energy.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple for the morning prayer ceremony – a deeply spiritual and culturally immersive experience. The temple is beautifully decorated with thousands of colorful lanterns. Afterward, explore the surrounding Insadong area for last-minute premium souvenir shopping – Korean celadon pottery, hanji paper crafts, and traditional lacquerware make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the scenic Seongbuk-dong neighborhood for a peaceful afternoon. Visit the Gilsangsa Temple, a serene Buddhist temple set in a forested hillside, and the nearby Choi Soon-dal House (a preserved traditional Korean mansion). Walk along the quiet, tree-lined streets of this upscale residential neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul – experience the unique Korean Christmas atmosphere. Seoul is festively decorated and Christmas Eve is celebrated as a romantic holiday. Head to Cheongdam-dong or the Lotte Hotel area for premium Christmas Eve dinner. Many luxury hotels offer special Christmas Eve dining events.

meals.breakfast: Café Bora (Insadong) – famous for their purple taro soft-serve and traditional Korean-inspired beverages and pastries.
meals.lunch: Sanchon Restaurant (Insadong) – revisit or try for the first time this exceptional temple food restaurant for a meditative, multi-course vegetarian feast.
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve dinner at the Grand Hyatt Seoul's Terrace Kitchen or the Shilla Hotel's La Yeon (three-Michelin-star Korean restaurant) – book well in advance as Christmas Eve dinners sell out months ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is one of the busiest nights in Seoul – restaurants and attractions will be packed. Book all Christmas Eve dining reservations well in advance. La Yeon at The Shilla Hotel is considered one of the finest Korean dining experiences in the world and requires advance reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas morning – enjoy a leisurely, indulgent hotel breakfast. Then visit the serene Deoksugung Palace, the only palace where you can see the Changing of the Royal Guard ceremony in front of a Western-style building. The palace grounds are beautiful in winter. Walk along the famous Deoksugung Stonewall Walkway (Doldamgil) – a romantic tree-lined path.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Seoul Museum of Art (SeMA) adjacent to Deoksugung for a premium contemporary Korean art experience. Explore the current exhibitions. Afterward, head to the upscale Cheongdam-dong area for luxury shopping at Korean designer boutiques and international luxury brands.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate Christmas evening with a premium Korean cultural performance. Attend a Nanta Show (non-verbal percussion performance) or a traditional Korean music and dance performance at the National Theater of Korea or the Korea House. End with a nightcap at a rooftop bar overlooking the Seoul skyline.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent hotel breakfast – treat yourself to the full spread on Christmas morning.
meals.lunch: Gwanghwamun area – Cheong Wa Dae Sarangchae café or a premium Korean restaurant near Deoksugung. Try Hadongkwan for premium gomtang (beef bone broth soup), a Seoul institution since 1939.
meals.dinner: Korea House (Pil-dong) – a premium cultural dining experience featuring a traditional Korean royal banquet followed by a traditional performing arts show. The ultimate combination of fine dining and cultural immersion. Reservations essential.

day_by_day.notes: Korea House offers combined dinner and performance packages – book in advance. The Deoksugung Changing of the Guard ceremony takes place at 11:00 AM and 2:00 PM (check schedule as it may vary on public holidays). Christmas Day is a public holiday in South Korea.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress – a UNESCO World Heritage Site just 30 minutes from Seoul by subway. The massive 18th-century fortress walls stretch 5.7km around the city of Suwon. Walk the full circuit of the fortress walls for panoramic views and a deep appreciation of Joseon Dynasty military architecture. Visit the Hwaseong Haenggung Palace within the fortress.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Seoul and visit the trendy Seongsu-dong neighborhood – often called 'Seoul's Brooklyn.' Explore converted factory spaces housing premium cafés, artisan workshops, concept stores, and galleries. Visit the Daelim Warehouse gallery and browse the unique boutiques along the main strip.
day_by_day.evening: Final major evening in Seoul – head to the Han River for a premium river cruise. Book a dinner cruise on the Han River for a romantic and scenic final evening, with views of Seoul's illuminated bridges and skyline reflected on the water. The Hangang Cruise offers premium dinner options.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before the early departure to Suwon.
meals.lunch: Suwon Galbi (Suwon-style short ribs) – Suwon is famous throughout Korea for its galbi. Visit Yeonpo Galbi or Hwaseong Galbi near the fortress for an authentic and premium local specialty.
meals.dinner: Han River Dinner Cruise – enjoy a premium set dinner while cruising past Seoul's iconic bridges. Book the premium class for the best experience. Alternatively, Ditto (Seongsu-dong) for a trendy, upscale dinner in the neighborhood.

day_by_day.notes: Suwon Hwaseong Fortress is accessible via subway Line 1 to Suwon Station, then a short taxi or bus ride. The full fortress wall walk takes approximately 2–3 hours. Dress in very warm layers as the fortress walls are fully exposed to the winter wind. Han River cruise tickets should be booked in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul – enjoy a relaxed farewell breakfast. Take a last stroll through the Bupyeong area near the hotel, visiting the Bupyeong Market for a final taste of authentic local Korean market culture. Pick up any last-minute souvenirs including Korean teas, premium ginseng products, Korean beauty items, and traditional snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, visit the Incheon Chinatown and Jayu Park area (close to the hotel) for a final cultural experience. Incheon's Chinatown is Korea's only official Chinatown and features unique Korean-Chinese fusion architecture and cuisine. Visit the Open Port Area with its preserved colonial-era buildings and the Incheon Art Platform.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Incheon International Airport for departure. Allow ample time for check-in, duty-free shopping (excellent Korean beauty, ginseng, and food products available), and a final Korean meal at the airport's premium dining options.

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast – visit a local haejang-guk (hangover soup) restaurant near the hotel for a hearty, warming bowl of kongnamul gukbap (bean sprout rice soup) or sundae gukbap – a true local farewell meal.
meals.lunch: Incheon Chinatown – try jajangmyeon (black bean noodles) and tangsuyuk (sweet and sour pork) at a traditional Incheon-style Chinese restaurant. This dish was invented in Incheon and is a must-try before departure.
meals.dinner: Incheon Airport Terminal 1 or 2 – dine at one of the premium airport restaurants. Bibigo or Bon Korean Restaurant in the departure terminal offer quality Korean cuisine for a satisfying final meal before your flight.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for airport check-in, security, and immigration at Incheon International Airport. The airport is consistently rated one of the world's best and has excellent duty-free shopping, lounges, and cultural experiences including a traditional Korean cultural center in the transit area. Consider purchasing premium Korean gifts at the duty-free: Sulwhasoo skincare sets, Korean red ginseng (KGC), and premium Korean teas make excellent souvenirs.

query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter from LAX
